column1: # kimiya — the isotope table behind spectroscopy::isotope_abundances (ADR 0002 #23, M4e-4): source data, typed from the
# publications below. scripts/oracle/src/t_spectroscopy.rs writes src/spectroscopy_data.cyr from it, scripts/oracle/
# validate.py re-checks it independently, and scripts/oracle/isotope_sources.py re-verifies it against fresh downloads of
# the sources (scripts/oracle/README.md). Retrieved 2026-11-10. Edit only to follow a source; then regenerate.
# Masses: AME2020, the unrounded atomic-mass table ("mass.mas20", file 1 of 4, DATE 3 Mar 2021).
#   M. Wang, W.J. Huang, F.G. Kondev, G. Audi and S. Naimi, "The AME 2020 atomic mass evaluation (II). Tables, graphs and
#   `mas20` is the nuclide's line, verbatim. Its format, from the file's header: a1,i3,i5,i5,i5,1x,a3,a4,1x,f14.6,f12.6,
#   f13.5,1x,f10.5,1x,a2,f13.5,f11.5,1x,i3,1x,f13.6,f12.6 (cc NZ N Z A el o, mass excess, binding energy per nucleon, beta-
#   decay energy, atomic mass, each with its uncertainty); the atomic mass is the i3 in u (columns 107-109) and the f13.6
#   in micro-u that follows (columns 111-123). `mass_u` is that mass in u with its published digits: "1 007825.031898"
# Abundances: TICE 2009, Table 1, column 9, "Representative isotopic composition (mole fraction)", pp. 399-402.
#   M. Berglund and M.E. Wieser, "Isotopic compositions of the elements 2009 (IUPAC Technical Report)", Pure Appl. Chem.
#   `tice` is the value as printed (its digit groups, and the expanded uncertainty of the last digits in parentheses);
#   `abundance` is its digits without the spaces and the uncertainty. 2H's footnote b ("Tank hydrogen has reported 2H mole
#   fractions as low as 0.000 032") is not part of the value.
# Why TICE 2009: CIAAW's current table, "Isotopic compositions of the elements 2024"
#   1ab770a48bb539d26ad2992a94b4c60d51743058b67f106796b754cd5035423b), gives these seven elements only intervals (H
#   [0.999 72, 0.999 99] for 1H, ...), so the 2009 single values remain their representative compositions; they are the
# Records, tab-separated; a `#` line is a comment.
# - isotope: Z, A, symbol, mass_u, abundance, tice, mas20. One per isotope, in Z then A order: kimiya 1.2.0's 16 and 36S.
# - interval: symbol, low, high, as printed, source: the element's CIAAW standard atomic weight interval, against which
#   validate.py checks its abundance-weighted mean mass. H and S, whose CIAAW pages were retrieved with the sources:
